en: So in order to show you how you could use a
framework like EVE for building AI agents, I
prepared a new project which you find
attached and we'll of course explore it in
greater detail soon.
Now, the idea behind EVE and many of these
frameworks is that you have pre-built
building blocks which you can compose
together to build an agent. In case of EVE,
that means that you simply set up a project
and install the EVE dependency in there.
So that is how you could create a new
project with Eve pre-installed in it.
And once you did that, in the case of Eve,
and it's different for every framework, but
in the case of Eve, you would use your file
system to construct an agent. So the Eve
package will scan the file system in which
it was installed, so your project, and will
look for a certain folder structure, certain
file names
to compose the agent, to build your agent.
For example, it will look for an agent.ts
file in an agent subfolder in your project.
And it will look into that file to find out
which model you want to use for your agent,
for example. So which AI model should power
the agent as a brain? It would look for
files in a tools folder in the agent folder
in your project. And every file in there
would register a new tool. And in that file,
you then need to have a certain structure.
You need to use the define_tool function
provided by that Eve package to define the
tool that should be loaded. But you don't
need to manually describe the tools to the
agent then
or manually set up this complex tool
registration which you saw earlier in the
course. Instead, the Eve framework will do
all of that for you. That is the idea. And
that's the general philosophy of Eve. I
won't turn this course into a complete Eve
course and you might also not be interested
in that. You also might not even be a
programmer and you might not be interested
in writing any code, and that's all fine.
That's just a general idea behind this
framework, and you'll find similar or
comparable ideas in other frameworks. Now
we'll just take a look at this codebase to
understand how things are wired together and
where we can find these building blocks you
learned about earlier in the course, or some
of them at least, and how you could run that
agent built with Eve here then.
